sections.title: Montana property tax: state rules

rows.label: Levied by
rows.value: Local governments (counties, cities, school districts and other taxing jurisdictions) set mill levies on state-certified taxable values
rows.note: Total mills from all jurisdictions are applied to the property's taxable value.

source.title: Montana Department of Revenue: Certified Property Values and Mill Levies

rows.label: State oversight
rows.value: Montana Department of Revenue, Property Assessment Division
rows.note: The State itself values taxable property statewide and certifies taxable values to local governments.

source.title: Montana Department of Revenue: Property Assessment Division

rows.label: Local levy growth limit
rows.value: Property tax revenue may grow by one-half of the average inflation rate over the past three years (plus newly taxable property)
rows.note: Sets each jurisdiction's maximum mills under MCA 15-10-420.

source.title: Montana Department of Revenue: Certified Property Values and Mill Levies

rows.label: Residential tax rates for primary homes and long-term rentals (2026)
rows.value: Tiered: 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value, 0.90% to $756,000, 1.10% to $1,511,999, 1.90% above; flat 1.90% for other residential property
rows.note: New state rate structure from 2026 that favours primary residences and long-term rentals over second homes and short-term rentals.

sections.title: Montana real estate transfer tax

rows.label: Real estate transfer tax
rows.value: None: the Montana Constitution prohibits the State and local governments from taxing the sale or transfer of real property
rows.note: Article VIII, Section 17, approved by voters on November 2, 2010 (Constitutional Initiative 105).
